title: Security changes, round 2: the four pieces you sent back

steps.path: When the assistant tries to send a form on a website
steps.headline: The send-a-form question is now the same permission card the chat uses for every other question.
steps.changed: It had its own boxed style. It is now the standard card: a header line, the question, then Yes, Always allow and No in the usual colours. Copied from the website-visit card.
steps.notice: It looks like every other ask. Buttons are Yes / Always allow / No. Behaviour is the same: Yes is one form, Always allow remembers the site.
steps.risk: Click only (no Enter key), as before. Other browser questions keep the old style; say if you want them moved too.

steps.headline: Sign out everywhere is now one short line and one button.
steps.changed: The long sentence and the long button are gone. It reads “Lost a device?” with a “Sign out everywhere” button, on the same kind of row as Sign out. Modelled on the Sign out row just above it, and on the delete-confirm strip in Local models.
steps.notice: The page is quieter. Nothing happens until you press the button; it then asks first (next slide).
steps.risk: The facts (it signs out this computer too, paired phones stay paired) are no longer visible until you press. They are in the confirm step, before anything happens.

steps.path: Account, then press Sign out everywhere
steps.headline: Pressing it shows the facts and asks you to confirm.
steps.changed: The row turns into: “Ends your YouCoded sign-in on every device, this one too. Phones paired for remote access stay paired.” with Cancel and Sign out everywhere.
steps.notice: Cancel puts the row back. Confirming signs this computer out as well. If the server cannot be reached, nothing changes and a short message says so.
steps.risk: One extra press compared with last round.

steps.path: Settings, Development, Report a bug, then Review ticket
steps.headline: The ticket review now has one short line saying it is public.
steps.changed: Three sentences became one: “Posted publicly on GitHub in itsdestin/youcoded — anyone can read it.”
steps.notice: Quieter. The “Sent with it” list below still shows what goes.
steps.risk: Dropped: “posted from your GitHub account” and “edits stay visible”.

steps.path: Browser panel, on a computer that blocks the browser’s extra protection
steps.headline: The “Extra browser protection is off” box is now a small chip with an X.
steps.changed: The big notice is replaced by a small amber pill, “Extra protection off”, with an X beside it. Modelled on the app’s status pills and the ✕ used in popups.
steps.notice: Almost no room taken at the top of the panel. The X hides it. Hiding lasts until you next open YouCoded, so it comes back once per launch and never nags while you work.
steps.risk: Because it is small, it is easier to ignore. That is the point, but the warning is real: the browser has less protection on that computer.

steps.headline: Pressing the chip opens the details and the fix; pressing it again closes them.
steps.changed: Under the chip: “This computer doesn’t allow the browser’s built-in protection against harmful websites. Pages still load, but be careful which sites the assistant visits. To turn it back on, allow ‘unprivileged user namespaces’ in your system settings.”
steps.notice: The picture below the chip moves down a little while it is open, and back up when you close it.
steps.risk: The fix step is technical; it is the only fix there is.

steps.path: docs/active/design/2026-10-13-ui-design-guide.md, new section “New UI stays standard and quiet”
steps.headline: Add these rules to the design guide so new screens stop arriving busy or one-off?
steps.today: The guide says to copy an existing surface and use the shared pieces, but nothing says a notice should be small, or how much copy a control may carry. The four pieces in this deck slipped through.
steps.problem: New screens keep arriving with their own styled boxes, long sentences on the page, and big notice boxes for things that do not block you.
steps.proposal: A new section with five rules, each tied to one of these examples: (1) copy an existing surface and its shared piece; no one-off cards (the form ask). (2) A notice that does not block you is a small amber chip with details on press and an X (protection off). (3) One short line per control; detail goes behind a press or a confirm step (sign out everywhere). (4) Say a fact once; do not repeat what the screen already shows (ticket review). (5) Before showing you new UI, the builder counts the boxes, sentences and buttons it adds. A test already checks that the form ask uses the shared card.
steps.risk: Rules are advice to future builders, not an automatic block; only the form ask has a test behind it so far.
